scores.evidence: The cloud database is synchronously copied across availability zones.
scores.rationale: Mostly correct on CDC, reverse CDC, read-your-writes, and proxy write hold; minor imprecision (RDS/Azure SQL MI reverse CDC and replication feasibility, DMS/Debezium claims, 'database-protocol proxy' holding writes) but no design-breaking errors.

scores.evidence: Reads never go down. Writes pause for 30 seconds or less, once, at cutover.
scores.rationale: Interprets zero downtime sensibly, covers integrations, batch, cutover, and explicit deferrals; vendor support/licensing and some clinical coordination are thin.

scores.evidence: There is one writable database at any moment... The application never writes to both databases.
scores.rationale: Consistent single-writer design with clear ownership; small loose ends such as a mid-plan tension about reads from replica vs writable and proxy on-prem dependency.

scores.evidence: 14 days in a row with zero unexplained reconciliation differences, p99 lag under 2 seconds
scores.rationale: Validation is risk-targeted with shadow diff, load tests, rehearsals, game day, and early slice; some thresholds are invented without being labeled provisional and rollback rehearsal is not explicit.

scores.evidence: I don't know these about your system yet; Phase 0, task 1 confirms them, and any difference changes the gates below
scores.rationale: Assumptions are explicit with revisit triggers; many numeric thresholds (5s, 300ms, 30s, RPO 5 min) are stated as defaults without basis or sensitivity.

scores.evidence: Otherwise a scheduler could book a slot, not see it on the replica, and double-book it.
scores.rationale: Covers silent drift, duplicate batch jobs, schema change, link drop, CDC stall, abort rules; lacks deeper treatment of malicious input and interface message duplicates/replay after cutover.

scores.evidence: Live cutover dashboard: lag, hold-queue depth, log-position match, write-pause timer.
scores.rationale: IaC, pipeline gates, domain-meaningful monitoring, abort rules, hypercare and rollback are concrete; incident ownership and staffing are only lightly addressed.

scores.evidence: Cost optimisation (reserved capacity, right-sizing) | 90 days of steady-state usage data.
scores.rationale: Cost is barely addressed beyond a build-vs-buy line and deferral; no drivers such as dual-running, private links, egress, or licensing.

scores.evidence: Changing database engines (e.g. Oracle → Postgres) | ... Never at the same time as the migration.
scores.rationale: Revisit triggers for each decision, reverse CDC rollback, deferred re-architecture, DNS indirection; lock-in to managed DB is noted with fallback.

scores.evidence: Keep the monolith as it is. The only new part is a strangler proxy in front of it.
scores.rationale: Rehost and minimal new components; proxy and shadow-diff are justified, with some ceremony (OpenTelemetry, pen test, 2 rehearsals plus game day) that is reasonable for a hospital.

scores.evidence: Each step has an abort rule. Before step (e), abort means setting on-prem back to writable
scores.rationale: Dependency-ordered phases with concrete tasks, exit checks, step-by-step cutover and revisit triggers; a team could start immediately.

checklist.evidence: BAA signed. Customer-managed encryption keys, TLS 1.2+ everywhere, PHI only over private links.
HL7 SIU (S12, S14, S15) and ADT feeds; patient portal and IVR/call centre; SMS reminders, billing/registration, reporting and the data warehouse
row counts and per-partition checksums every 15 minutes, with full-table checksums nightly.
There is one writable database at any moment.
Keep reverse CDC running and on-prem warm for 30 days as a tested rollback path.
Two redundant dedicated private links (Direct Connect / ExpressRoute) on separate physical paths, plus an encrypted VPN as a backup.
up to 5 minutes of data loss, back up within 1 hour
Connect on-prem Active Directory to Entra ID/Okta, with MFA and break-glass accounts.
Mirror 100% of read traffic and compare the answers. Load-test at the real peak (Monday 8 a.m. call-centre surge, ×2).
Brief nursing supervisors, the ED and the call centre... Run the production cutover in a low-volume window (e.g. Sunday 03:00).
take a final encrypted archive under the hospital's records-retention policy, get a certificate of media destruction

traps.evidence: Change data capture (CDC), one database writing at a time... At least 2 full rehearsals in staging
The application never writes to both databases.
Map every dependency: HL7 SIU (S12, S14, S15) and ADT feeds
No code changes during the migration.

note: Strong, safety-focused single-writer CDC migration with concrete phases and cutover runbook; weak on cost, vendor licensing, and an explicit rollback rehearsal, and thresholds are unjustified.
